problems.problem_text: Two fair coins are tossed. List all possible outcomes in the sample space.
problems.solution: Each coin can be H or T. The sample space is {HH, HT, TH, TT}.

problems.problem_text: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting exactly one head?
problems.solution: Sample space: {HH, HT, TH, TT}. Outcomes with exactly one head: HT, TH = 2 outcomes. P = 2/4 = 1/2.

problems.problem_text: A spinner with numbers 1, 2, 3 is spun and a coin is tossed. What is the probability of getting (3, Heads)?
problems.solution: Sample space: {(1,H),(1,T),(2,H),(2,T),(3,H),(3,T)} — 6 outcomes. Only (3,H) is favourable. P = 1/6.

problems.problem_text: Two fair dice are rolled and their scores are added. How many outcomes give a total of 5?
Two fair dice are rolled. Using a sample space diagram, find the probability that both numbers are the same (a double).
Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the sum of the two numbers is 8 or more.
A fair coin is tossed and a fair six-sided dice is rolled. Find the probability of getting a head and an even number.
problems.solution: Sample space has 12 outcomes. Favourable: (H,2),(H,4),(H,6) — 3 outcomes. P = 3/12 = 1/4.

problems.problem_text: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the sum of the two numbers is a prime number.
problems.solution: Total outcomes = 36. Prime sums: 2,3,5,7,11. Sum=2: 1 way. Sum=3: 2 ways. Sum=5: 4 ways. Sum=7: 6 ways. Sum=11: 2 ways. Total = 15. P = 15/36 = 5/12.

problems.problem_text: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the number on the first dice is greater than the number on the second dice.
problems.solution: P(first > second) = P(first < second). P(first = second) = 6/36 = 1/6. So P(first > second) = (1 - 1/6)/2 = 5/12.

problems.problem_text: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the sum of the two numbers is a multiple of 3.
problems.solution: Total outcomes = 36. Multiples of 3 sum: 3(2 ways), 6(5 ways), 9(4 ways), 12(1 way). Total = 12. P = 12/36 = 1/3.

problems.problem_text: Two fair dice are rolled and the difference between the two scores (larger minus smaller) is recorded. Find the probability that the difference is exactly 3.
Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the sum of the two numbers is at most 9.
problems.solution: Total outcomes = 36. Sum > 9 means sum = 10(3 ways), 11(2 ways), 12(1 way): total 6. P(sum <= 9) = 1 - 6/36 = 30/36 = 5/6.

problems.problem_text: A bag contains red (R) and white (W) cards. Two cards are drawn from the bag. The sample space is {RR, RW, WR, WW} all equally likely. Given that exactly one card is red, find the probability that the first card is red.
problems.solution: Given exactly one red: outcomes are RW and WR. Of these, 1 has first card red (RW). P = 1/2.

problems.problem_text: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the product of the two numbers is at least 18.
Three fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the sum of the three numbers is 10.
problems.solution: Total outcomes = 6^3 = 216. Count ordered triples with sum 10: a=1:4, a=2:5, a=3:6, a=4:5, a=5:4, a=6:3. Total = 27. P = 27/216 = 1/8.

problems.problem_text: Two fair tetrahedral dice (numbered 1 to 4) are rolled, and the two numbers showing on the base are recorded. Find the probability that the sum of the two numbers is a prime number.
problems.solution: Total outcomes = 4 × 4 = 16. Prime sums: 2(1 way), 3(2 ways), 5(4 ways), 7(2 ways). Total = 9. P = 9/16.
